CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT

May 4, 2022 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Until further notice, meetings of the Inglewood Planning Commission will
be conducted pursuant to California Government Code section 54953(e),
which allows the City to use teleconferencing for members of the public
to access a meeting and to address the legislative body via a call-in
option.

CALL-IN OPTION
1. Members of the public who wish to attend the Planning Commission
  Meeting of May 4, 2022 and address the Planning Commission must use
  the call-in option noted below:
  Instructions: Dial one of the Phone Numbers below and when
  prompted, enter the Access Code:
  Phone Number: 888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 2428751#
In the event of a disruption which prevents the City from broadcasting
the meeting to the public using the call-in option, or in the event of
a disruption within the City’s control which prevents the public from
offering public comments using the call-in option, the Planning
Commission shall take no further action on items appearing on the meeting
agenda until public access to the meeting via the call-in option is
restored.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City also provides alternative methods for members of the public to
submit comments and/or to observe a public meeting.  The following
alternative methods are provided to the public as a matter of convenience
only and the disruption in service to any alternative method does not
preclude the Planning Commission from taking further action on an agenda
item.  In the event of a disruption to any alternative method below
members of the public should use the call-in option above.
2. Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public
may choose to submit comments for consideration by the Planning
Commission by sending them to Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager at
mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of
the Planning Commission prior to consideration of the agenda, comments
must be received prior to 12:00 P.M. on the day of the meeting.
Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments
received after 12:00 P.M. and prior to the close of the public hearing
will be made part of the official public record of the meeting.
3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
   On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video.
  Please check with your cable provider for details
   Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video
  at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

Accessibility: If you will require special accommodations due to a
disability, please contact the Planning Division Office at (310) 412-
5230, One Manchester Boulevard, 4th Floor, Inglewood, California 90301.
All requests for accommodations must be received 48 hours prior to the
day of the hearing.
Spanish: "Si no entiende esta noticia o si necesita más información,
favor de llamar a este número (310) 412-5230."

Pages]

4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to address

  public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  Minutes approval for April 6, 2022, Planning Commission meetings.

6.  PUBLIC HEARING
  a. A public hearing to consider an application by Ben Moradzadeh
  for Special Use Permit No. 2022-001 (SP-2022-001) to allow a
  1,023 square-foot addition and exterior and interior alterations
  to an existing nonresidential structure that exceeds twenty
  thousand dollars ($20,000.00) on an approximately 17,000 square-
  foot, C-2 (General Commercial)/MEOZ (Medical Enterprise Overlay)
  zoned property at 945 South Prairie Avenue.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2022-002; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving SP-2022-001
  subject to 20 conditions, and/or add conditions as deemed
  appropriate.
  The applicant has requested that this item be postponed to the
  Planning Commission Meeting of June 1, 2022.

  b. A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment No. 2021-003
  (ZCA 2021-003) to establish regulations for Hookah Lounges.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2021-053; and
  2) Adopt a Resolution Recommending approval of Zoning Code

  Item 6b documents

7.  Public Comments

8.  Commission Initiatives.

9.  Adjournment.

In the event that the Planning Commission meeting of May 4, 2022, is not
held, or is concluded prior to a public hearing or other agenda item
being considered, the public hearing or non-public hearing agenda item
will automatically be continued to the next regular Planning Commission
meeting.

Hearing materials are available at:
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-Commission-4 and
at City Hall, 1st Floor Lobby Information Desk during regular business
hours. If any additional documents are received for distribution to the
Planning Commission after the publication of this Agenda but before 12:00
P.M. on the day of the meeting, they will be made available for public
inspection at the following webpage:
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-Commission-4.

(Note: The above procedures are subject to change for future Commission
meetings. Please refer to future Planning Commission agendas for public
participation option procedures at that time.)

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, MAY 4, 2022

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, May 4, 2022, in the City Council
Chambers, on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge
of Allegiance by Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams, the meeting
was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams
Excused
Absence: Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager

Staff:  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., ECDD Director
  Bernard McCrumby, Acting Planning Manager
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Christine Rivera, Assistant Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Mr. McCrumby, Acting Planning Manager announced that staff has
received no communications from the public, but staff has made a
few minor modifications to the Ordinance coming before you this
evening, which has been provided to you and a copy has already
been uploaded to the City’s Website.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

(5) MINUTES APPROVAL:
Chairman Springs called for a vote to approve April 6, 2022
minutes.

Motion to Approve April 6, 2022 Minutes by Commissioner Trejo and
second by Commissioner Rice.

The motion passed with the following roll call vote:
Ayes:  Commissioners Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.
Abstained:  Commissioner Patrick
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
May 4, 2022

(6) NON-PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6A: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2022-001 (SP-2022-001), 945 SOUTH
PRAIRIE AVENUE.

A public hearing to consider an application by Ben Moradzadeh for
Special Use Permit No. 2022-001 (SP-2022-001) to allow a 1,023
square-foot addition and exterior and interior alterations to an
existing nonresidential structure that exceeds twenty thousand
dollars ($20,000.00) on an approximately 17,000 square-foot, C-2
(General Commercial)/MEOZ (Medical Enterprise Overlay) zoned
property at 945 South Prairie Avenue.
The applicant has requested that this item be postponed to the
Planning Commission Meeting of June 1, 2022.

6B: ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 2021-003 (ZCA-2021-003), REGULATIONS
FOR HOOKAH LOUNGES CITYWIDE.
A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment No. 2021-003
(ZCA 2021-003) to establish regulations for Hookah Lounges.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff –
 For clarification, is this ordinance for Chapter 12 of the City
  of Inglewood’s Municipal Code for the consideration to establish
  new guidelines if the City is to add any new Hookah Lounges?
 Just wanting to understand why is this item coming before the
  planning commission and for what purpose.
 Also she stated that she noticed the comparison of Hookah
  Lounges and Smoke Shops is often used, are there any smoke shops
  here in Inglewood already and if so, where are they?
   Ms. Fewell responded to Commissioner Patrick’s questions.
   Mr. McCrumby also responded to Commissioner Patrick’s
  question.
 As we are comparing Hookah Lounges to Cafés per the present
  code, will this mean that some Hookah Lounges will be serving
  food to their patrons?
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 Also for clarification, what is the deal or difference between
  a Smoke Shop and a Hookah Lounge, they’re both dealing with
  smoking, correct?
   Mr. Jackson, Sr., responded to Commissioner Rice’s
  questions.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 Also needing clarification on what is the purpose of a hookah
  lounge?
 Are Hookah Lounges used to pedal marijuana into a smoke pipe
  and pass it among its participants?
 Last, per the staff report, there are two licensed smoke shops
  already here in the City of Inglewood, does this statement
  mean that there are some illegal Hookah Lounges here in
  Inglewood?
 When applicants come into the City to apply for their business
  licenses did they truthfully state that they were opening an
  actual Hookah Lounge?

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
May 4, 2022

  With the Hookah Lounge being compared to a Café, has any Hookah
  Lounge attempted to state that they were going to open a Café,
  and then switch from a Café to Hookah Lounge?
  Was the purpose of this new code amendment regarding Hookah
  Lounges and smoke shops a result of IPD having such a difficult
  time with illegal Hookah Lounges operating at all hours of the
  evening such as past 1:00am and 2:00am, along with trespassing
  and  illegal  activity  by  the  participants  of  these
  establishments who were not licensed to operate in the first
  place?
  Next question is if we the planning commission approve this
  zoning code amendment, will it require the present licensed
  Hookah Lounges to have to modify their present activities in
  order to stay operating?
   Ms. Fewell responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.
   Mr. Jackson, Sr., responded to Commissioner Trejo’s
  question.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the Planning Commission for
further comments and or questions.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 Concerned about the size of the Hookah Lounge buildings and
  that if they are being compared to Café’s because of the
  parking ratio’s, that it will possibly hinder any new Hookah
  Lounge business from opening here in Inglewood, because at
  present there are no buildings with a large enough parking
  area to allow the Hookah Lounge to operate within the code’s
  specifications and requirements, thus causing any new Hookah
  Lounge business to fail.

Chairman Springs asked the operator to open the phone lines for
the public to comment For or Against this item.

FOR / AGAINST:
None, confirmed per the AT&T Operator.

Chairman Springs seeing none, asked the Planning Commission for a
motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Rice made the motion to affirm categorical exemption
EA-CE-2021-053, and adopt the attached resolution recommending
City Council adoption of Zoning Code Amendment No. 2021-003 (ZCA-
2021-003), with two additional conditions, 1. Change the hours of
operation to 9:00am until 11:00pm and 2. Require an increased
parking ratio of 300 square feet for every 1 parking space and 3.
No Loitering Outside of the Hookah Lounge to keep all patrons
inside of the Lounge and was seconded by Commissioner Shaw-
Williams,

Mr. Pan, Assistant City Attorney made a statement to the Planning
Commission regarding a California Labor Code, Labor Code Section
6404.5 that there will be no smoking in a work place, and if the
planning commission limits the Hookah Lounges to only “In-Doors”,
there will be very looming circumstances in operating the Hookah
Lounge, which is why the Lounge is being kept open during business
hours, this is why they are set up in this manner.

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
May 4, 2022

Commissioner Rice asked the question –
 What’s the difference between the Hookah Lounge and a Cigar
  Club?
   Mr. Pan responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.
   Mr. Jackson also responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Chairman Springs stated that with this information he asks that
Commissioner Rice withdraw his motion and Commissioner Shaw-
Williams withdraw her second of the motion.

Commissioner Rice has withdrawn his initial motion and the second
to the motion was withdrawn by Commissioner Shaw-Williams.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 With any motion that is made at tonight’s meeting, will any new
  Hookah Lounges be required to follow these new guidelines and
  procedures including parking and hours of operations?
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff –
 The present two Hookah Lounges will they have to adhere to the
  new hours of operation, also what are their current hours of
  operation, and also, if they close will they have to abide by
  these new regulations?
   Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked staff –
 If these present Hookah Lounges have issues with code
  enforcement and have too many infractions, will their licenses
  be revoked and then if they attempt to start up a new Hookah
  Lounge will they then be subject to the new requirements?
   Mr.  Jackson  responded  to  Commissioner  Shaw-Williams’
  question.

Chairman Springs asked staff and/or the Assistant City Attorney –
 Per Commissioner Patrick’s question as to why wouldn’t the
  current Hookah Lounges have to conform to the new regulations?
   Mr. Jackson responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

Chairman Springs stated that there are no more questions and that
it is time for a motion for this Zoning Code Amendment?

MOTION:
Commissioner Rice made the motion to affirm categorical exemption
EA-CE-2021-053, and adopt the attached resolution recommending
City Council adoption of Zoning Code Amendment No. 2021-003 (ZCA-
2021-003), with two additional conditions, 1. Change the hours
of operation to 9:00am until 11:00pm and 2. Require an increased
parking ratio of 300 square feet for every 1 parking space and
was seconded by Commissioner Shaw-Williams, that Resolution No.
1929

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AND
  RECOMMENDING TO THE CITY COUNCIL FOR APPROVAL
  ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 2021-003 (ZCA-2021-
  003), TO ESTABLISH REGULATIONS FOR HOOKAH
  LOUNGES CITYWIDE.

Be approved.

  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
May 4, 2022

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Yeas:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

Mr. McCrumby explained there is no appeal process, and that the
recommendation will go directly to the City Council for
adoption.

(7) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None, (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

Chairman Springs closed the hearings to the public and asked for
the Planning Commission Initiatives.

Chairman Springs wished everyone a good evening and adjourned
